newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie surges on AUD/CAD bids, tempts fate.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie surges on AUD/CAD bids, tempts fate.

text.p: *AUD staged wild 1.3-cent short covering rally overnight as heavy buying of AUD/CAD triggered a tide of stop loss bids
*Bounce improved awful chart picture, scope seen to $0.7630 *Growing feeling RBA will not cut this week, but A$ rally itself may make bank more confident about moving now
*May goods and services data at 11.30 am should not disturb

By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) a dazed local dollar was resting at US$0.7544/49 having climbed all the way from US$0.7453/58 late here Monday. This was its best start since June 12, the day it fell over 1/2 cent in reaction to dire May employment data.

There was some talk the AUD/CAD buying had been on behalf of George Soros, although many were sceptical noting sharp moves in anything from the rand to the yuan were often attributed to him. The rally past US$0.7530 went a little way to repairing the technical damage done by last week's break of US$0.7470 support, but analysts cautioned the currency needed to clear US$0.7575/80 to confirm a real bottom had formed.
On the crosses the A$ stormed back to C$1.0402/13 having been down at five month low of C$1.0259/70 late here Monday.

The bounce recouped much of the losses suffered in the wake of last week's surprise rate hike by the Bank of Canada. Traders said the rally could reflect a fund shift from Canadian to local bonds since Australia was one of the few western economies still on an easing track.

The RBA's policy board holds its monthly meeting today and analysts put the chance of another cut at around 50 percent, although an increasing number think the bank will hold off for more data and perhaps ease late in the month or early August.

It is not unkown for the RBA to move on the morning of a meeting -- its did so in January 1990 and September 1991 -- but it had not done so in recent years, expressing an intention to move the day after a meeting when possible.
In this case the timing was made difficult by a Federal Reserve meeting on Wednesday, which could just see U.S. rates hiked, so analysts were not ruling out Thursday either.
Today's data on the balance of goods and services was expected to show a surplus of A$163 million in May, but will likely be ignored by a market obsessed with monetary policy.
